# The branch introducing sesam got squash-merged, and a branch stacked on it is
# merged afterwards. The audit log has no git merge base (git hands an empty
# %O), yet both sides share its history, so the merge must still go through.

mv a.txt $TMPDIR/a.txt
mv b.txt $TMPDIR/b.txt
exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'
exec git commit --allow-empty -m root

exec git checkout -b intro
exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
cp $TMPDIR/a.txt a
exec sesam add a --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'intro sesam'

exec git checkout -b stacked
cp $TMPDIR/b.txt b
exec sesam add b --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'stacked: add b'

exec git checkout master
exec git merge --squash intro
exec git commit -m 'squashed intro'

exec git checkout stacked
! exec git merge master -m 'merge master'
! stderr 'missing key line'
stderr 'audit log was therefore semantically merged'
exec git commit -m 'merge master'

exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/b.sesam
stdout 'BBB'

# Back onto master: its mainline anchors at the squash commit instead.
exec git checkout master
! exec git merge --no-ff stacked -m 'merge stacked'
exec git commit -m 'merge stacked'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- a.txt --
AAA
-- b.txt --
BBB
